comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose significant year-over-year revenue growth in their primary Data Center/Compute segments for fiscal year 2024, driven by AI infrastructure demand. NVDA reports a 266% growth in Compute revenue, specifically attributing it to higher shipments of the Hopper GPU platform for LLMs and generative AI. Similarly, AMD reports a 94% increase in Data Center net revenue, driven by higher sales of its Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs. While both companies cite AI-specific hardware (GPUs) as the primary growth driver, NVDA highlights a much higher percentage growth rate (266% vs 94%) and specifies the Hopper platform's role in inference and training, whereas AMD broadly cites both GPU accelerators and CPUs.

sentences.text: Compute grew 266% due to higher shipments of the NVIDIA Hopper GPU computing platform for the training and inference of LLMs, recommendation engines and generative AI applications.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.
